tools.name: address_profile
tools.description:
One-call US property report for an address or coordinate: FEMA flood zone (SFHA, base flood elevation, FIRM panel), county demographics, and 10-year hazard history (FEMA disaster declarations, NOAA storm events, USGS earthquakes), with a plain-English summary and a source for every part.

Everything

tools.name: admin_areas
tools.description:
State and county for a coordinate, with Census GEOIDs. Free - answered from boundaries the platform ingests and holds, with no provider call.

Point-in-polygon against Census TIGER/Line boundaries (§22.2). Returns the administrative areas containing the point, most specific first, each with the GEOI

tools.name: area_demographics
tools.description:
Population and median household income for the county containing a point, from American Community Survey 5-year estimates.

Composes two ingested datasets (§22.2): TIGER/Line resolves the coordinate to a county GEOID, then the ACS layer is read by that key. Pass `geoid` directly to skip the boundary

tools.name: census_geocode
tools.description:
Free. Turns a US street address into a latitude/longitude plus the state, county and census tract it is in (with GEOIDs), using the U.S. Census Bureau geocoder. Use it first, then pass the point to the paid property tools.

One-line address to point, with the Census Bureau's own match: the matched a

tools.name: flood_zone
tools.description: FEMA flood zone for a US address or coordinate: zone (A, AE, VE, X ...), whether it is in the Special Flood Hazard Area (where lenders generally require flood insurance), base flood elevation with its datum, FIRM panel and effective date, NFIP community, and any Letter of Map Revision. Live from FEM

tools.name: hazard_history
tools.description: Natural-hazard history for a US county or address: FEMA declarations (major disasters, emergencies and fire management, by type, with links), NOAA storm events with deaths and reported property damage by type and year, and USGS earthquakes within 100 km since 1950. One call, each source reported apa
